title: Zscaler's GCP Terraform package for Cloud Connector: image, NICs, Pub/Sub Editor, FIPS and zsec defects

prose.text: Zscaler's GCP Terraform package (direct modules, example roots and the zsec helper) is the documented way to deploy Cloud Connector on GCP. Its layers carry different defaults and some defects; none of them is a Cloud Connector service behavior unless a claim says so.

{{pubsub-editor-default}} {{pubsub-editor-byo}} {{zsec-wds-prompt}} {{wrapper-pubsub-defaults}} Workload discovery is the feature that needs the role: [[cloud-connector.gcp.workload-discovery:pubsub-editor-required]].

checks.do: Whether grant_pubsub_editor is set as intended for the root in use, since most example roots default it to true and the grant is project-wide.
Whether the rendered user data is valid JSON before deploying base_cc_ilb or cc_ilb with Secret Manager credentials.
Which ZIP object the Cloud Functions were built from after an ASG zsec run that chose an existing bucket object.

image-table.statement: The CCVM module README lists image zs-cc-ga-2-08132026 in project mpi-zscalercloudconnector-publ with release date 8/28/2026, marking it and zs-cc-ga-03092026 with `*` as the minimum required for Auto Scaling, and marks images zs-cc-ga-02022025 and zs-cc-ga-10292023 (`**`) as deprecated as of April 15, 2026.

quotes: *This release in the minimum required for Auto Scaling support
**Support for deploying these images are deprecated as of April 15, 2026

example-image-default.statement: The example roots look up the image in project mpi-zscalercloudconnector-publ unless `custom_image_name` is set, with `marketplace_image` defaulting to zs-cc-ga-2-08132026 and described as Zscaler recommending the latest image for new instances.

quotes: description = "Available marketplace image name to deploy. Zscaler recommends always deploying new instances with the latest image" default = "zs-cc-ga-2-08132026"

instance-template.statement: The CCVM module's instance template enables IP forwarding and lists the service subnetwork as the first network interface and the management subnetwork as the second.

quotes: network_interface { subnetwork = var.vpc_subnetwork_ccvm_service } network_interface { subnetwork = var.vpc_subnetwork_ccvm_mgmt }

user-data-metadata.statement: The module passes the user data to the VM as the `ZSCALER` metadata key, and the example roots build it as JSON with `cc_url`, `http_probe_port`, `fips_enabled` and `gcp_service_account`, plus `secret_name` for Secret Manager or `hcp_vault_addr`, `hcp_vault_secret_path`, `hcp_vault_role_name` and `hcp_gcp_auth_role_type` for HashiCorp Vault.

pubsub-editor-default.statement: In the IAM service-account module, `grant_pubsub_editor` defaults to true and is described as granting roles/pubsub.editor to the CCVM service account at project scope.

quotes: variable "grant_pubsub_editor" { type = bool default = true description = "If true, grant roles/pubsub.editor to the CCVM SA at project scope" }

pubsub-editor-byo.statement: When enabled, the module creates the project IAM binding for roles/pubsub.editor on either the service account it creates or a caller-supplied (bring-your-own) one, so supplying an existing account does not avoid the grant.

quotes: count = var.grant_pubsub_editor && var.byo_ccvm_service_account == "" ? 1 : 0 project = var.project role = "roles/pubsub.editor"

# When caller brings their own SA (full email) resource "google_project_iam_member" "ccvm_editor_byo_sa" { count = var.grant_pubsub_editor && var.byo_ccvm_service_account != "" ? 1 : 0 project = var.project role = "roles/pubsub.editor"

zsec-wds-prompt.statement: The `zsec` helper asks whether to enable Workload Discovery Service integration, warning that it grants roles/pubsub.editor project-wide to the VM service account; its default answer is no, which exports `TF_VAR_grant_pubsub_editor=false`, and yes exports true.

quotes: Enable Workload Discovery Service (WDS) integration? This grants roles/pubsub.editor project-wide to the CC VM Service Account. Only enable if WDS is required.

wrapper-pubsub-defaults.statement: The example roots default `grant_pubsub_editor` to true in `base_1cc`, `base_1cc_zpa`, `base_cc_asg`, `base_cc_asg_zpa`, `base_cc_ilb`, `base_cc_ilb_zpa` and `cc_ilb`, and to false only in `cc_asg`.

fips-examples.statement: All eight Cloud Connector example roots (`base_1cc`, `base_1cc_zpa`, `base_cc_asg`, `base_cc_asg_zpa`, `base_cc_ilb`, `base_cc_ilb_zpa`, `cc_asg`, `cc_ilb`) declare `fips_enabled` and write it into both the Secret Manager and HCP Vault forms of the JSON user data.
fips-examples.conditions: Search of each example root's variables.tf and main.tf at the pinned commit for fips_enabled; two roots are quoted.

zsec-fips.statement: The `zsec` helper asks whether to enable FIPS mode and exports `TF_VAR_fips_enabled` as 'True' or 'False'.

quotes: Enable FIPS mode for this Cloud Connector deployment? (yes/no):

direct-module-no-fips.statement: The direct CCVM module takes generic `user_data` and has no `fips_enabled` input, so FIPS coverage is a property of the example roots and helper, not of the module.
direct-module-no-fips.conditions: Search of the CCVM module's variables.tf at the pin for fips; only the user_data input is quoted.

quotes: variable "user_data" { type = string description = "Cloud Init data" }

ilb-userdata-defect-code.statement: In `base_cc_ilb` and `cc_ilb`, the default (Secret Manager) user data at the earlier pin put `"gcp_service_account": ...` with no trailing comma directly before `"fips_enabled": ...,`, which itself ended with a comma before the closing brace; at the current pin `fips_enabled` comes before `gcp_service_account` in both, so the last entry carries no comma.

quotes: # Populate potential local map with default GCP Secret Manager
# Populate potential local map with default GCP Secret Manager

evidence.after: # Populate potential local map with default GCP Secret Manager
# Populate potential local map with default GCP Secret Manager

ilb-userdata-invalid.statement: With the default `hcp_vault_enabled = false`, those two roots therefore rendered user data that was not valid JSON (a missing comma and a trailing comma) at the earlier pin, and `terraform validate` does not parse heredoc content, so it did not catch it. This was an example defect, not a service FIPS or JSON behavior.
ilb-userdata-invalid.conditions: JSON grammar applied to the quoted heredoc; Terraform's treatment of heredocs as opaque strings is not quoted from a registered source.

zsec-zip-checksum.statement: When `zsec` downloads a missing Cloud Function ZIP, it fetches the selected URL's .sha256 companion, compares it with a local SHA-256 and deletes the ZIP and exits on mismatch; if no checksum file is published it only warns that integrity cannot be verified and continues.

quotes: Cloud Function ZIP file appears to be missing from directory ${dtype}/function_zip. Trying to download now...
SHA256 checksum MISMATCH — aborting to prevent supply-chain compromise.${RESET}" rm -f "$dtype/function_zip/${zip_name}" exit 1
**Warning** SHA256 checksum file not published at remote. Integrity cannot be verified.${RESET}" fi echo "export TF_VAR_cloud_function_source_object_name=$zip_name" >> .zsecrc

existing-object-branch.statement: When `upload_cloud_function_zip` is false, the Cloud Function module skips the upload and looks up an existing bucket object named by `cloud_function_source_object_name`, from which the functions are built.

quotes: # Or reference an existing storage object (implying that both the bucket AND object zip file exists already) data "google_storage_bucket_object" "existing_cloud_function_zip_object" { count = var.upload_cloud_function_zip ? 0 : 1 name = var.cloud_function_source_object_name

zsec-quoted-condition.statement: In `zsec`, answering yes to whether the Cloud Function ZIP is already in an existing bucket sets `upload_function_zip=false` and exports the object name, but the ZIP download loop's condition quotes the whole expression `"$upload_function_zip == true"`, and the loop then writes the downloaded or locally selected ZIP's name and path to `cloud_function_source_object_name` and `cloud_function_source_object_path`.

quotes: Is the latest Cloud Function version ZIP file already uploaded to this bucket? (yes/no):

zsec-zip-flow-reentered.statement: Because a quoted non-empty string is always true in a bash `[[ ]]` test, an ASG `zsec up` run enters the ZIP flow even after the operator chose an existing bucket object, and can replace the chosen object name with a local or downloaded ZIP's name while the upload flag stays false, so the module may look up a wrong or nonexistent object. This is a helper defect, not Cloud Connector runtime behavior.
zsec-zip-flow-reentered.conditions: Bash test semantics applied to the quoted condition; not run.

invalid-userdata-outcome.title: Cloud Connector VM outcome with invalid JSON user data
invalid-userdata-outcome.detail: The base_cc_ilb and cc_ilb roots render invalid JSON user data by default; whether the Cloud Connector bootstrap rejects it, tolerates it, or fails to register is not established by a source read.
invalid-userdata-outcome.blocks: diagnosing ILB example deployments whose connectors do not register
